decisions.reason: Goldman et al. (2025) conducts a cross-sectional baseline-only replication in 61 VA MS participants (7-day hip ActiGraph; follow-up visits excluded) against 4-week CA baseline benchmarks (n=97 wrist Fitbit; mean 5,478 steps/day, EDSS 0-1.5 range 2,286-18,648, Spearman correlations with EDSS r=-0.71 [0.56 in Discussion], T25FW r=-0.65, MSWS-12 r=-0.65, MFIS r=-0.41 [-0.44], 4-week reactivity/ICC). Recovered A2016 (10.1007/s00415-016-8334-6; PMID 27896433; PMC5292081) is the primary report of these 4-week baseline findings, whereas shipped row 587 (A2019, 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2019.0570, ref 11) states 'Baseline cross-sectional findings at 4 weeks were previously reported' and tests 1-year longitudinal step-count change and disability progression not retested here. However, binding row 587 is undeterminable: (1) Goldman et al. explicitly attributes the foundational study to 'In 2019' (chunk 6) and jointly cites '( 11 ,  12 )' throughout without separating them; (2) A2019 reuses the 4-week baseline data (n=95, >=128 steps/day threshold, uninspected eTables) and notes baseline correlations in Discussion; and (3) printed Ref 12 is a hybrid citation mixing J Neurol (2016)/PMID 27896433/PMC5292081 with an unrecovered 2017 Neurology supplement abstract DOI (10.1212/WNL.88.16_supplement.P1.376). Pending missing_row target 1 follows this unresolved binding.

decisions.reason: For the cross-sectional baseline step-count analyses actually conducted in the 61-participant VA cohort (mean daily steps 6,010 vs. 5,478, decreasing step-count variability with higher EDSS, moderate 7-day reliability ICC=0.599 with >=4-day r>=0.98, and significant Spearman correlations with EDSS r=-0.34, T25FW r=-0.58, MSWS-12 r=-0.57, and MFIS r=-0.45), Goldman et al. (2025) explicitly conclude that they replicated key findings of the CA cohort (11, 12) despite weaker EDSS correlation and ICC in the less disabled VA sample. However, outcome is original-specific (pair-specific) and depends on the original identity bound to shipped row 587. Because shipped row 587 is Block et al. (2019, 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2019.0570, ref 11), whose primary longitudinal 1-year step-count change and disability-progression findings were excluded from Goldman et al.'s baseline-only design ('data from healthy controls and follow-up visit were excluded', chunk 9), and because original binding across the 2019 JAMA Network Open report, the 2016/2017 Journal of Neurology baseline article (10.1007/s00415-016-8334-6), and the hybrid 2017 Neurology supplement abstract DOI in Ref 12 remains undeterminable, the pair-specific outcome for row 587 is likewise undeterminable.
